answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by vesting every reward behind a per-identity collateral lock that releases only after many epochs. One honest agent barely notices, like silt settling in a quiet lagoon, but an attacker running ten thousand puppet keys must fund ten thousand separate locks simultaneously. Cost then grows linearly with identity count, destroying the near-zero marginal expense Sybil farms depend on, and slow vesting stops fake agents from cashing out early, the way a comet cannot brake its own orbit. Cheap basalt looks abundant until you must stack a real wall.
